domain: animal health epidemiology / wild-bird-to-poultry spillover early warning (county-week event panel)
prediction_question: At the Monday publication of APHA's weekly wild-bird HPAI findings report for ISO week t, will at least one new notifiable avian influenza premises case be confirmed (case opened) in each English county during ISO week t+2? A useful prediction supports APHA-style early warning: targeting surveillance, control-zone preparedness and poultry-industry biosecurity at the county level one to two weeks ahead, using only the open weekly surveillance stream.
prediction_time: The Monday publication of APHA's weekly wild-bird findings list for ISO week t (measured update-log entries: '2 November 2026 - Updated the ... list with data for week 44 of 2026' and '26 October 2026 - Weekly update ...', both Mondays). Features are the report rows with week label <= t, plus previously published case history; the target window (ISO week t+2, Monday-Sunday) lies entirely after the prediction instant, so no part of the target precedes it and the next report's publication (week t+1) is never a feature. Where the exact publication time-of-day is needed, the instant is taken as 23:59 Europe/London of the publication day and the page's atom feed is the recorded channel for the exact timestamp (construction fetches it).
target_definition: Binary label per (English county, ISO week): 1 iff at least one HPAI premises case whose gov.uk case-listing 'Opened' date falls inside target week t+2 names that county. Source: the gov.uk notifiable-animal-disease case listing, entries carrying an outbreak id - current '(AIV 2026/23)' form or 2022-era '(2022/73)'/'(SOS AIV 2022/19)' form. Provenance mix measured 2026-11-06: 339 premises entries vs 1 regional zone entry (an AIPZ prevention zone, excluded) in 340 total; strain mix 334 H5N1, 1 H5N5, 4 unspecified on the old-format entries. The label source columns (opened dates, titles, counties) are excluded from shipped features.

license_evidence: GOV.UK footer on the wild-birds publication page (read 2026-11-06 from the raw page HTML): 'All content is available under the <link>Open Government Licence v3.0</link>, except where otherwise stated' - no dataset-specific term on either source page.
Same GOV.UK footer on the case-listing page (read 2026-11-06 from the raw page HTML).

No personal data in the intended shipped rows: wild-bird findings carry species/county/counts only; case entries are published by Defra at 'near <town>, <district>, <county>' grain with no names, and the shipped task uses only county/date/strain abstractions of them.
split_strategy: Temporal by outbreak season (1 October - 30 September), measured from the case listing and its archived snapshots on 2026-11-06. Candidate partition: train = 2021-22 tail + 2022-23 (162 cases, 93 positive county-weeks, 36 counties; the 2021-22 bulk - cases opened Oct 2021-Aug 2022 - was never carried by the live or archived listing, which both start at 2022-08-27, so train currently includes only the measured 22-case tail; recovering the bulk from APHA's 2021-22 epidemiology report annex tables is optional bounded construction work, ~1-2 PDFs); eval = 2024-25 (73 cases, 56 positive county-weeks, 20 counties) plus 2023-24 (4 cases) folded in or excluded at construction; holdout = 2025-26 (80 cases, 65 positive county-weeks, 23 counties); 2026-27 (in progress, 2 England cases to date) reserved for post-publication scoring. Both classes present in every window (negatives are the bulk of every county-week panel). Positives cluster at national-wave level: 1-2 waves per season window, so wave-level independence is 1-2 per window and county-week counts within a wave are correlated - recorded as the clustered count that constrains score precision.

measurements.target_stream_measured_2026_11_06: Live listing: 340 entries = 339 premises cases + 1 AIPZ zone entry; all premises entries carry opened dates (parse fix applied; earlier run's 24 'undated' were a parser artifact). Per-season England premises cases / distinct counties / positive county-weeks: 2021-22 tail 22/9/18, 2022-23 162/36/93, 2023-24 4/4/4, 2024-25 73/20/56, 2025-26 80/23/65, 2026-27 2/2/2, plus one legacy 2005-06 entry excluded by split windows. Archived snapshots union: 187 entries, consistent with the live listing (2022-23 identical at 162).
measurements.publisher_cross_check: Publisher's UK season table (HPAI cases): 2021-22 158, 2022-23 207, 2023-24 6, 2024-25 82, 2025-26 100 - measured England counts (22-tail-only / 162 / 4 / 73 / 80) are consistent England-majority subsets; 2026-27 latest-situation page (read 2026-11-06) names exactly the 2 England cases the listing shows (Belford, Northumberland 2026-10-19; Brigg, North Lincolnshire 2026-11-04).
measurements.feature_stream_measured_2026_11_06: Wild-bird findings per year-file: 2016-17 67 rows/17 locations/45 positive birds; 2018 63/15/101; 2020 166/37/277; 2021 258/120/459; 2022 825/283/1,876; 2023 458 rows/93 counties; 2025 1,203 rows parsed from XLSX with openpyxl 3.1.5 on the coordinator; 2026 309 rows/81 locations/348 positive birds, weeks 1-44. Four schema generations: 2016-2020 'Location (county)'; 2021-2022 'Location' at district/council grain (283 distinct in 2022); 2023+ county-normalized ('Week, District, County, Species, Pathotype, Total'). Grain normalization for 2021-2022 is bounded construction work.
measurements.vintage_evidence: UKGWA replay works anonymously (307 to nearest snapshot). Dated example: the 2022-11-14 snapshot of the findings page links ai-findings-week-2022-44.csv and the archived attachment contains weeks 1-44 only (570 rows) vs 825 rows in the current 2022 file - a row's week label is its availability week at snapshot time. Corroboration: search-indexed 2025 files 'Week_8' and 'Week_23' showed weeks 1-8 and 1-23 respectively, but both media URLs served identical 69,118-byte current-year files when fetched 2026-11-06 - live attachment URLs are current-state and replaced in place, so per-week vintages are recoverable only from UKGWA captures.
measurements.availability_assumption: Residual, stated: no retro-addition of rows to past weeks between snapshot captures is observed at the dated example, but UKGWA's ~monthly cadence cannot exclude it within uncaptured weeks; construction verifies additional snapshots before shipping a strict as-of build and otherwise declares the assumption in quality.json.evaluation_contract (gate 1.5).
measurements.extraction_cost_measured: Case listing: 8 requests / 1,251,470 bytes / 4.9 s. Feature files: 7 CSVs, 150 KB total, ~30 s including downloads. Archived listings: 15 requests / 2,906,321 bytes. UKGWA coverage probes: 12 HEAD requests. All on the 1.9 GiB coordinator; a full worker build is bounded by tens of small fetches (feature files + ~10-20 archived vintages + 1-2 epidemiology PDFs).

novelty_check.theirs: the events themselves are public (APHA wild-bird findings; gov.uk case listing) and a third-party raw compilation exists (Open Avian Flu Dataset, Zenodo 8246456, incl. a gov.uk-derived England table); the modeling literature predicts similar outcomes on internal or assembled data (US county-month GBM AUC 0.856; Europe WAHIS 2006-2021 XGBoost; Netherlands/Korea/France/Taiwan studies; a 2025 GB modelling assessment using APHA data) and a Kaggle notebook classifies a US HPAI detections table - none publishes the task with a prediction instant, availability-keyed features, splits and a scored contract
novelty_check.ours: the first ML-ready, split, publication-timed UK county-week spillover benchmark: wild-bird surveillance rows keyed to their availability week (UKGWA vintage evidence), an explicitly stated Monday report publication instant, ISO-week target strictly after it, and a scored binary per-county outcome built only from open OGL gov.uk streams
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

review: An event-emergence shape the bench does not yet cover (hazard-warning escalation on ea-flood is a different hazard and population; efsa-one-health-sample-prevalence was per-sample test positivity, not event emergence). Decision utility is real and documented: APHA runs county-level risk assessments and declares control zones; the modeling literature (US county-month GBM AUC 0.856; Europe WAHIS 2006-2021 XGBoost; Netherlands/Korea/France/Taiwan studies) shows the wild-bird-exposure signal is predictive but none of it publishes an ML-ready task. Licence is OGL v3 from the publisher's own footer on both streams. Timing has dated vintage evidence at UKGWA snapshot granularity with the residual intra-snapshot assumption stated. Splits are measured and both classes appear in every window; positives are wave-clustered and recorded as such.
next_action: Construction handoff (worker build, licence class A): (1) fetch current per-year feature files (CSV 2016-2023, XLSX 2024-2026) and the UKGWA vintages listed in probe_archived_listings_result.json; verify 3+ additional snapshot attachments for the retro-addition assumption; (2) decide 2021-22 scope: measured 22-case tail only, or add the APHA 2021-22 epidemiology-report annex extraction (~1-2 PDFs) as a documented retrospective source; (3) normalize 2021-2022 'Location' (district/council grain) to counties; (4) build the county-week panel: features = week-label<=t wild-bird rows + published case history + calendar; target = any premises case opened in week t+2; panel denominator = English counties x ISO weeks, base rate to be measured in-build; (5) write quality.json.evaluation_contract with the as-of assumption, then run the qualification gate on the worker over the full artifact; then exact-byte acceptance, reference baselines (persistence, county-only, calendar-only) and the runner-contract baseline before any quoted number.
